newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Approval of ABN's SFB buy delayed - report.
newsitem.headline: Approval of ABN's SFB buy delayed - report.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Reserve Board has delayed a decision on ABN AMRO NV's $1.9 billion acquisition of Standard Federal Bancorp after a complaint from a U.S. investor, the Wall Street Journal reported.

It said the regulator's decision on the purchase would be delayed until mid-April because of the complaint that the Dutch bank defrauded American investors of up to $88 million when it underwrote a bond issue by Dutch truck maker DAF NV.
The newspaper said the transaction would probably have been approved next week if there had been no opposition.
It quoted Anne Phillips, an assistant vice-president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, as saying she had referred the matter to the Federal Reserve Board in Washington.
This is a standard practice after a public protest against a bank merger.
But the newspaper also quoted an unnamed ABN AMRO spokesman as saying the bank still expected full clearance of the deal by the middle of this year.
DAF went bankrupt in 1993 before being resurrected and sold.
In January, a Dutch court rejected two legal actions by DAF bond investors against ABN AMRO and other banks.
